intro: Lesson 10: The Bronze Age: metal and trade. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Where did the metal come from?
points: Copper from mines like the Great Orme, Wales

model.title: Why did Wales and Cornwall trade?

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Each place had what the other needed

blocks.text: Draw trade routes for tin, flint and bronze with arrows.

keywords.def: the time when people made tools from bronze
a metal made by mixing copper and tin
a place where rocks and metals are dug out
a round home with a pointed roof

questions.q: Why was a bronze axe better than a stone one?
questions.a: Sharper, stronger, and it could be melted and remade

questions.q: Where in Britain was tin found?
Core: Draw arrows on the UK map to show copper and tin travelling to make bronze. Add a key.
questions.a: Arrows from Wales (copper) and Cornwall (tin) with a key

questions.q: Extend: Write a sentence: 'Trade helped people because ...'
questions.a: For example: they got metals they did not have

questions.q: Stretch: Who might have become rich in the Bronze Age? Why?
questions.a: People who controlled mines or trade routes, because everyone needed metal
B) Copper and tin. Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.

questions.q: Big question: how could a new metal change people's lives?
questions.a: Better tools and weapons, more trade, and some people became rich and powerful
